scenarios.name: carbon_roof_on_wagon
scenarios.change: MY27.1 carbon roof released for wagon
rules_added: R3 only on S1, C1, W1

impact.change: MY27.1 carbon roof released for wagon

scenarios.briefing: The MY27.1 change releases the carbon roof (R3) for the wagon, replacing the rule "R3 only on S1, C1" with "R3 only on S1, C1, W1." This adds 78 buildable configurations (1644 to 1722) and removes none, so no configuration in the current plan becomes invalid (0 configs, 0 cars). The plan was left as it is: the mix still uses 107 configurations with an unchanged gap of 140, all 600 orders are kept with 0 replaced, no kept car moves day or is resequenced, and there are 0 supplier call-off changes. Nothing in the rules or the plan blocks the change, but the plan does not yet use it either, since carbon roof volume stays at 50 before and after. Ask order intake to confirm actual wagon carbon roof orders, then rerun the mix with the 78 new configurations to see whether they reduce the gap of 140, keeping in mind that any added R3 wagons would create new call-off changes.

scenarios.name: new_highway_pilot
scenarios.change: MY27.1 highway pilot A2 launched (electric only, EU+US)
rules_added: US cars must carry A1 or A2

impact.change: MY27.1 highway pilot A2 launched (electric only, EU+US)

scenarios.briefing:
The MY27.1 launch adds the highway pilot (A2) as an electric-only option for EU and US. US cars may now carry either the driver assistance pack (A1) or A2 instead of being required to carry A1. This raises buildable configurations from 1644 to 1860 (216 added, none removed), and no configuration in the current plan becomes invalid.

The plan absorbed A2 by replacing 61 orders and keeping 539. That brings A2 to 60 cars and lowers A1 from 419 to 359, while configurations in use rise from 107 to 119. No kept car changes day and only 3 are resequenced, giving 64 supplier call-off changes in total.

The main constraint is that A2 requires the electric powertrain (P3), which stays fixed at 200 cars. All A2 volume must therefore come from those 200. The mix gap also widened from 140 to 184, so the revised mix sits further from target than before.

Before releasing the 64 call-off changes, review whether the 61 replacements can be chosen to avoid widening the mix gap from 140 to 184.

scenarios.name: sport_seats_need_sport_trim
scenarios.change: MY27.1 sport seats now only with sport trim

impact.change: MY27.1 sport seats now only with sport trim

scenarios.briefing: For MY27.1, sport seats (S2) can now only be built with sport trim (T2), where they previously also allowed premium trim (T3). This cuts buildable configurations from 1644 to 1456, removing 188 with none added, and makes 11 configurations in the current plan invalid, covering 72 cars. The plan kept sport seats steady at 167 cars, shifting trim from 193 to 191 premium and from 198 to 200 sport. In doing so it replaced 142 orders, kept 458, moved no kept cars to a different day and resequenced 1, for 143 supplier call-off changes in total. The new rule itself is the only blocker in the input: sport seats with premium trim can no longer be offered, while the mix gap stayed at 140 both before and after, and configurations in use rose from 107 to 128. Since 142 orders were replaced although only 72 cars were invalid, we recommend re-running the plan with all still-valid orders locked so that only the affected cars change, which should reduce call-off changes and limit the spread to more configurations.
